needs_review: AUTH IS WRONG AND PROVEN WRONG (kept as scaffolded only because this wave's rule says keep scaffolded auth; DO NOT PROMOTE until fixed): the spec sends a request header literally named 'DeepL-Auth-Key'. DeepL's official OpenAPI security scheme is name='Authorization', in=header, value 'DeepL-Auth-Key <api-key>'. The live shape-proof run caught it verbatim: GET /v2/usage answered 403 with {"message":"Missing Authorization header, expected 'Authorization: DeepL-Auth-Key <API key>'"}. The fix is auth {"type":"header","header":"Authorization","template":"DeepL-Auth-Key {{api_key}}"}. SHAPE_PROVEN in the proof file means host, TLS and paths are proven; it does NOT mean this connector can authenticate, and with this header it cannot.

HOST SPLIT (unresolved by this spec): DeepL serves Pro keys at https://api.deepl.com and Free keys at https://api-free.deepl.com, and both are listed as servers in the official OpenAPI document. A Free key ending in ':fx' sent to the Pro host is rejected, so this connector as written works for Pro keys ONLY. The base_url is fixed to the Pro host this wave; a follow-up should either template the host off the key suffix or expose it as a credential field (the schema supports base_url {template}/{fromCredential}).
shape-proof was run against the Pro host only. The Free host is unprobed here, so nothing in the proof file speaks to api-free.deepl.com.

read-only wave: /v2/translate, /v2/document, /v2/write/rephrase and all glossary create/delete calls are POST or DELETE and are deliberately NOT exposed. Translation is billed per character, so it is excluded under the read-only rule rather than because it is inexpressible.
no clamps declared: none of these three endpoints take a page-size or limit parameter, so there is no numeric input to clamp. truncate 2000 bounds the payload instead.
